Bill.BriefDescription: Concerning self-supporting, fee-based programs at four-year institutions of higher education.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to self-supporting, fee-based programs at four-yearinstitutions of higher education; and adding a new section to chapter28B.15 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 28B.15 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) When a decision is made to establish a new selfsupporting,feebased degree program or change a degree program that is supportedby state funding to a program that is selfsupporting and feebased,the governing boards of the state universities, regional universities,and The Evergreen State College shall notify enrolled and prospectivestudents and undergraduate and graduate student government associationsat least six months before implementation with an estimate of tuitionand fees. (2) The governing boards of the state universities, regionaluniversities, and The Evergreen State College shall each establish acommittee comprising of administrators, faculty, and students to createcriteria upon which to base decisions for moving statesupported degreeprograms to selfsupporting programs. p. 1 HB 1669 (a) Criteria to be considered must include, but not be limited to,the following: (i) Whether moving the program to a selfsupporting program willresult in the loss of student financial aid; (ii) Whether the program prepares students for careers in publicservice, such as public health, nursing, and librarianship, amongothers; (iii) Whether the program is designed to serve professionaladvancement, and serves students who are already employed and on acareer track; and (iv) The median income in the field of preparation. (b) The committee that creates the criteria for establishing selfsupporting, feebased programs shall establish a process for movingselfsupporting, feebased degree programs that do not meet thecriteria to programs that receive state funding.
